newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex charges dumping vs Romania, Bulgaria cos.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex charges dumping vs Romania, Bulgaria cos.

text.p: Mexican steel company Hylsamex SA de CV plans to level dumping charges against Romanian and Bulgarian steel companies, a company official told Reuters on Wednesday.

"We are in the process of gathering information and all the necessary elements, but the problem exists and we are going to press charges," said Rafael Rubio, assistant director of economic studies and international marketing at the Monterrey-based firm.
He said products targetted in the dumping charge include cold and hot rolled sheet and cut-to-length steel plate.

He would not say which companies in both countries were the target of the investigation, but added that they are easily identifiable "because there are only one or two and they are still state-owned."

Rubio added Hylsamex had been investigating imports from both countries during the past year and had noticed "prices that were very low, perhaps 20-30 percent lower than the average import prices from other nations."

Imports of cold rolled steel from Romania grew to 6,400 tonnes during 1996 from 600 tonnes the year before, while imports of steel plate from Bulgaria mushroomed to 3,500 tonnes last year compared to 470 tonnes in 1995.
